preamble: /d/ becomes voiceless [θ] by spirantization plus devoicing, almost always at the end of a word or before a voiceless consonant. In the Madrid area word-final /d/ is often [θ] (Madrid [maˈðɾiθ], sed [seθ]), and Old Spanish d before a consonant gave modern z /θ/ (judgar > juzgar). Gothic did the same: the fricative allophone [ð] of /d/ was devoiced to þ [θ] word-finally after a vowel (gōþs 'good' beside genitive gōdis).

examples.note: Colloquial realization of word-final /d/ as [θ] in Madrid and its surroundings, alongside standard [ð̥] or zero.
Same word-final realization; nonstandard outside central Spain.

examples.from: Old Spanish judgar 'to judge' (< Latin iūdicāre)
examples.note: Diachronic: the [ð] allophone of /d/ before a voiced consonant merged with /θ/ (also Old Spanish yedgo > yezgo 'dwarf elder').
After a vowel and before a voiceless consonant or word end, /d/ was devoiced to þ [θ].
